title: AI and Automation Lead for Cyber Application Compliance - VP
description: Who we are looking for An experienced Artificial Intelligence Compliance & Automation Lead who will play a critical role in modernizing and scaling the firm's Cyber Application Compliance Program through the strategic use of artificial intelligence, machine learning, automation, and advanced analytics. This individual will lead the development and integration of AI-enabled solutions that improve compliance monitoring, risk identification, evidence collection, reporting, workflow efficiency, and regulatory alignment across the enterprise application portfolio. The ideal candidate will possess a combination of technical expertise, software development experience, cybersecurity and compliance knowledge, and the ability to translate complex business requirements into scalable AI-driven solutions. Experience within highly regulated industries, particularly financial services, is strongly preferred. Other key relationships: Cyber Application Compliance Teams Information Security Risk Management (ISRM) Cybersecurity Governance, Risk & Compliance (GRC) Enterprise Architecture Cloud Engineering & DevOps Teams Application Owners and Technology Leaders Data & Analytics Teams ServiceNow IRM Platform Teams Compliance, Risk Management, Legal, and Internal Audit Technology and Business Executives What you will be responsible for Lead the adoption and integration of artificial intelligence capabilities across the Cyber Application Compliance Program. Design, develop, and implement AI-driven automation solutions to improve compliance operations, risk assessment activities, and regulatory reporting. Identify opportunities to reduce manual effort through intelligent workflows, machine learning models, predictive analytics, and process automation. Partner with cybersecurity, compliance, risk, technology, and business stakeholders to integrate AI capabilities into existing governance processes. Develop AI-assisted compliance monitoring capabilities to identify control deficiencies, policy exceptions, and emerging risks. Design and maintain complex integrations between governance platforms, compliance systems, security tooling, data repositories, and reporting solutions. Build scalable data pipelines and automation frameworks that improve the quality, accuracy, and timeliness of compliance evidence collection. Utilize advanced analytics and AI techniques to improve cyber risk visibility and support executive decision-making. Enhance the organization's ability to manage compliance against cybersecurity frameworks, including NIST, regulatory requirements, and internal standards. Develop AI-enabled dashboards, metrics, key risk indicators (KRIs), and predictive reporting capabilities. Support implementation of intelligent workflows within platforms such as ServiceNow, Archer, cloud environments, and other enterprise technologies. Evaluate emerging AI technologies and develop practical use cases that improve operational effectiveness and control maturity. Collaborate with technical teams to establish responsible AI governance practices, security standards, and model oversight processes. Ensure AI-enabled solutions align with the firm's cybersecurity, privacy, legal, and risk management requirements. Analyze large and complex datasets to identify opportunities for process improvement, risk reduction, and compliance optimization. Translate business objectives into technical specifications and solution designs. Communicate complex AI concepts, technical architectures, and compliance implications to both technical and non-technical audiences. Create and deliver executive presentations, implementation roadmaps, and business cases supporting AI investments. Partner with technology and compliance teams to establish automation strategies that support regulatory examinations, audits, and internal reviews. Stay current on developments in artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, automation technologies, regulatory expectations, and industry best practices. Mentor and guide team members in AI adoption, automation opportunities, and advanced analytics capabilities. What we value These skills will help you succeed in this role: Deep understanding of artificial intelligence, machine learning, generative AI, large language models (LLMs), and intelligent automation technologies. Strong software development and coding experience with modern programming languages such as Python, Java, C#, JavaScript, or similar. Experience designing, developing, and deploying enterprise-grade AI solutions. Ability to understand and optimize complex end-to-end business and technology processes. Strong analytical and strategic thinking capabilities. Experience integrating data from multiple enterprise systems and platforms. Knowledge of cybersecurity governance, risk management, compliance, and control frameworks. Familiarity with NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF), NIST SP 800-53, NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF), and related industry standards. Experience dev

title: Enterprise and Operational Risk Director
description: Experian is a global data and technology company, powering opportunities for people and businesses around the world. We operate across a range of markets, from financial services to healthcare, automotive, agribusiness, insurance, and many more. Experian invests in people and new advanced technologies to unlock the power of data. We have an amazing team of 25,200 people in 32 countries. The Director, Risk supports Experian's Financial Services and Data business within the North America Data Office. This role leads risk, regulatory compliance, and data privacy efforts to help the business meet applicable federal and state requirements and industry guidelines. The Director partners with Compliance, Audit, Legal, Product, Sales, and other North America business units to strengthen governance and support compliant products and cross-business initiatives. At Experian, we believe great work happens when people come together. We're focused on attracting talent in and around our designated hub locations who are open to collaborating with colleagues in person. Aligning employees to these talent markets helps foster collaboration, strengthen team connections, and support long-term career growth within Experian. You will report to the SVP, Data Governance and reside in or near our North America Headquarters in Costa Mesa, California. You will have opportunity to: Lead risk management and regulatory compliance initiatives across the Financial Services and Data business unit. Partner with Product and Sales teams to develop products and services that meet regulatory requirements. Develop and maintain compliance policies, procedures, standards, and employee training programs. Establish processes to identify, assess, monitor, and report compliance risks. Develop corrective action plans to address compliance issues and reduce operational risk. Advise internal teams and clients on regulatory compliance, data privacy, and privacy impact assessments. Collaborate with Legal, Audit, Compliance, and other business units on shared regulatory and governance initiatives. Lead and develop a team responsible for supporting risk management and compliance activities. 8+ years of experience in compliance and risk management. 3+ years of experience in data privacy. Experience applying federal and state laws and regulations relevant to financial services, consumer data, and privacy. Working knowledge of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA), Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA), Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) requirements, Federal Trade Commission (FTC) requirements, Federal Communications Commission (FCC) requirements, Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA), and California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA). Experience developing compliance or audit reports for governing bodies, legal entities, or external authorities. Experience developing or maintaining compliance policies, procedures, standards, or corrective action plans. Experience advising business teams on regulatory compliance, data privacy, or privacy impact assessments. Experience leading, coaching, or developing employees. Benefits/Perks: Our uniqueness is that we celebrate yours. Experian's people first, inclusive and purpose driven culture is multi award-winning; World's Best Workplaces™ 2025 (Fortune Global Top 25), Great Place To Work™ in 26 countries to name a few. Check out Experian Life on social or explore our Careers Site to understand why. Our compensation reflects the cost of labor across several U.S. geographic markets. The base pay range for this position is listed above. Within this range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors such as job-related skills, experience, and education. You will be also eligible for a variable pay opportunity. Experian is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer for all groups protected under applicable federal, state and local law, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know at the earliest opportunity. Benefits/Perks: Great compensation package and bonus plan Core benefits including medical, dental, vision, and matching 401K Flexible work environment, ability to work remote, hybrid or in-office Flexible time off including volunteer time off, vacation, sick and 12-paid holidays Explore all our exciting benefits here: https://myexperianbenefits.com/ Recruitment Fraud Awareness - Experian's recruitment process is conducted only through authorised channels. Recruitment communications will only be sent from an @ experian.com email address. Experian will never ask candidates to make any payment as part of an application, interview, assessment, onboarding, or recruitment process. To apply for roles or verify opportunities, please visit experian.com/careers . #LI-Hybrid

title: Recruiting Operations Program Manager
description: Datadog’s Recruiting Operations team is on a mission to scale and optimize the Recruiting organization through operational efficiency, best-in-class tooling, analytics, and programs. We are looking for a Program Manager to own our sourcing tools and workflows and to build the capability that lets our sourcers find and engage the people who will build the next decade of Datadog. In this role, you will own our sourcing tech stack end to end. Today that means Gem as our candidate relationship management system and LinkedIn Recruiter as our primary sourcing channel, but you will own the question of what the stack should be: which tools we invest in, which we retire, how they fit together, and how they connect into Greenhouse. You will set the roadmap, hold the vendor relationships and renewals, define how sourcing performance is measured, and partner with sourcing leadership to turn a collection of tools into a genuine competitive advantage in how Datadog finds talent. AI is changing sourcing faster than any technology shift in the last decade, and we want someone who is excited to be at the front of it. Our platforms are shipping AI capability continuously — assisted search, drafted outreach, agentic workflows — and much of it is genuinely useful while some of it is not. You will be the person who tells the difference, decides what Datadog adopts, designs the workflows that put it to work, and makes sure we use it in a way that is fair to candidates and defensible to regulators. Datadog builds for the AI era; we want our recruiting function to operate like it. through them, drive real adoption of the CRM across the team, and tell us honestly where we are leaving capability on the table. You will also work with the owner of our ATS to make sure data flows cleanly from sourcing into the hiring pipeline. At Datadog, we place value in our office culture — the relationships and collaboration it builds, and the creativity it brings to the table. We operate as a hybrid workplace to ensure our Datadogs can create a work-life harmony that best fits them. title: Head of Risk Malaysia and Thailand
description: Head of Risk Malaysia and Thailand At AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as a Head of Risk Malaysia and Thailand to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team. Make your mark in Enterprise Risk Management The Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) team partners across the AIG organization, facilitating rational risk-taking that drives profitable growth. ERM is responsible for ensuring that our organization has the right tools, processes, and systems in place to identify, measure and manage these risks. The team plays a critical role in strategic decisions about where to expand or contract businesses, where to invest to collect premiums that are enough to cover future claims, and how much capital we need to reserve to weather unexpected events. It also helps the enterprise to develop effective controls that support the successful execution of organizational strategy. As an ERM colleague, you will shape and support how AIG manages its risks. Your knowledge about the company’s risks will shape the daily decision-making among AIG’s businesses and functions, while informing our clients and the markets that we serve. You will also have the opportunity to enhance your risk and business acumen as we continue to navigate an ever-changing risk environment. ERM advocates a healthy risk culture, encouraging our diverse colleagues to speak up when we spot something that fosters risk so that we can address it effectively. About the role What you need to know: The role of the Head of Risk is to maintain a robust risk management framework that is appropriate for the size, business mix and complexity of AIG Malaysia and Thailand, is in line with AIG policies and meets regulatory expectations. Job Duties & Responsibilities Responsible for the overall management and execution of the risk management strategy and activities. Maintain an effective risk management framework to identify, assess, manage, monitor and report all material risks that AIG Malaysia is exposed to. Adequate support of the Board of Directors and the CEO in meeting their responsibilities with respect to the protection of policyholders and the management of the risk profile of the company. Facilitate quarterly management’s Risk and Capital Committee meetings. Engagement with the regulator on a needs basis. Maintenance of AIG Malaysia’s Risk Appetite Statement, KRIs, Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment process, top and emerging risks. Oversight over the implementation of the Operational Risk Management (ORM) framework, including facilitating the Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) annual work plan, maintaining the Risk Event capture and reporting program, Key Risk Indicators, etc. Strengthen the risk culture to underpin the effectiveness of the overall risk management framework. Risk reviews of material outsourcing, major initiatives and business development (e.g. new products, business plan). Timely escalation of any risk matters to Malaysia and Thailand management, within the ERM function and to the Board as needed. Participate in and contribute to APAC and Global ERM/ORM initiatives. (e.g. International Center of Correspondence, eGRC rollout for APAC, etc) Designated Senior Officer accountable for overseeing the effective management of climate-related risks and ensuring climate deliverables are met, in accordance to BNM expectations. Team talent development Key Measuring Parameters Implementation of ERM initiatives in an effective and efficient way Support local management in the whole risk management process including but not limited to identification, assessment, monitoring, and mitigation etc. by using qualitative and quantitative tools What we’re looking for: Experience preferably in broad scope of Risk Management; or experience in general insurance industry operations; Minimum Bachelor’s degree. Partially or fully qualified in Actuarial, ERM, CFA or other related profession is an added advantage; Excellent communication skills in both oral and written English; Self-motivated and can drive initiatives independently; Have flexibility to work in a dynamic, multinational and challenging environment. #LI-SK1 At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike. Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family. title: Program Manager, AV Safety Policy & Programs
description: At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive. Lyft is building the safety capability for autonomous mobility. As Program Manager, AV Safety Policy & Programs, you'll own key parts of Lyft's AV Safety Management System (SMS) across all four pillars: Safety Policy, Safety Risk Management, Safety Assurance, and Safety Promotion. You'll also make sure the processes, documentation, and cross-functional machinery behind them work in practice. This is a high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of safety policy, program design, and cross-functional process support. You'll author policy, run risk and review cadences, turn safety data into decisions, and keep the Safety Review Board (SRB) running. You'll work closely with AV partners, and you can speak credibly about AV safety with technical counterparts, senior leaders, and external partners. Responsibilities: Safety Policy: Own Lyft's AV safety policy framework, safety procedures, and partner-facing governance documentation, including version control and periodic review cycles. Maintain governance charters, committee operating rhythms, and escalation protocols. Safety Risk Management: Run hazard identification and risk assessment for AV operations and new launches. Maintain the operational risk register and track mitigations to closure. Safety Assurance: Track safety performance indicators and trends, and surface emerging risks. Participate in incident and near-miss investigations and own corrective action (CAPA) tracking, so findings feed back into policy, operations, and partner work plans. Coordinate evidence and remediation for audits and certifications. Safety Promotion: Drive safety communications, lessons-learned documentation, and training readiness. Safety Review Board: Run the SRB cadence, including agendas, materials, decision records, and follow-through on action items. Partner Engagement: Contribute to the standards and assessment frameworks Lyft uses with AV partners, and support partners' safety assurance and risk management activities. Program Execution: Drive AV safety programs with safety leaders, including partners across EHS, Operations, Engineering, Legal, and others from inception through go-live. This includes safety readiness for new market launches and partner integrations. Experience: 4+ years supporting or managing safety management programs in a safety-critical transportation industry (AV, aviation, rail, automotive, trucking, or equivalent) Working knowledge of SMS principles and how they apply to AV operations Hands-on experience with risk assessment, incident follow-up, and corrective action tracking Strong technical writing, including policy, procedures, and partner- or regulator-facing materials  Comfort with safety data, including tracking indicators, spotting trends, and presenting findings to technical and senior audiences Proven ability to run multi-stakeholder programs without direct authority Bachelor's degree in safety, engineering, policy, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience Nice to Have Familiarity with AV safety frameworks (e.g., AVSC best practices) and US AV reporting requirements Experience supporting robotaxi, ridehail, or fleet operations Experience operating in a matrixed, partner-dependent environment where safety policy must be implemented through influence rather than direct control Exposure to multi-market or international safety operations Benefits: Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled Mental health benefits Family building benefits Child care and pet benefits 401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future In addition to 12 observed holidays, salaried team members have discretionary paid time off, hourly team members have 15 days paid time off 18 weeks of paid parental leave. Biological, adoptive, and foster parents are all eligible Subsidized commuter benefits Monthly Lyft credits and complimentary Lyft Pink membership Lyft is an equal opportunity employer committed to an inclusive workplace that fosters belonging. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, age, genetic information, or any other basis prohibited by law. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Lyft highly values having employees working in-office to foster a collaborative work environment and company culture. This role will be in-office on a hybrid schedule — Team Members will be expected to work in the office 3 days per week on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays. title: Director of People Programs, Systems & Analytics
description: About the Job: LaunchDarkly is looking for a Director, People Programs, Systems & Analytics to establish operational objectives, roadmaps, work plans, and operating rhythms for People programs, systems, analytics, and AI, translating the People Operations strategy and LaunchDarkly’s priorities into executable plans. Your team will develop technical and AI-assisted capabilities while  turning workforce data into analytics and insights that allow the business to make informed decisions. This role reports to the Senior Director, People Operations. In this role you will lead a small team and establish the framework for responsible AI use regarding People data. You will partner with Legal, Security, and IT, and recommend solutions that improve reporting, employee support, and efficiency. Responsibilities: Design the vision, strategy, roadmap, governance, and operating rhythms for all People programs, systems, analytics and AI, in alignment with LaunchDarkly’s business and People priorities. Manage the orchestration and successful completion of organization wide deliverables including OKRs, annual deliverables, and key projects, acting as a visible leader and facilitator within the People organization. Lead, coach, and develop a small, high-performing team, creating clarity, strong partnerships, and a culture of thoughtful execution and continuous improvement. In partnership with the Director, People Operations, ensure that programs and operating processes across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, offboarding, employee data, documentation, compliance-related workflows, employee support, and international operations can be optimally managed through our HR tech stack with measurable, decision-informing analytics Design and evolve the People technology ecosystem, ensuring systems are integrated, scalable, secure, fit for purpose, and aligned to the employee and business experience. Establish standards for People data quality, definitions, governance, access, documentation, and stewardship, and build trusted reporting and self-service insights for People partners and business teams. Design an analytics strategy that translates workforce data into executive-ready narratives and practical recommendations across headcount, attrition, hiring, organizational health, employee experience, and workforce planning. Define a responsible AI strategy for the People function, including use-case prioritization, governance, human oversight, and adoption of solutions that improve reporting, decision-making, employee support, and operational efficiency. Partner with the Senior Director, People Operations, functional partners, and subject-matter experts to translate capability gaps into scalable learning experiences, then measure participation, effectiveness, behavior change, business impact, and equity of access. Lead change management for new systems, programs, policies, and processes, including communications, training, stakeholder readiness, adoption, and post-launch improvement. Manage vendors, dependencies, and tradeoffs, bringing structure to ambiguity and maintaining a clear view of value, risk, and long-term scalability. Qualifications: 15+ years of experience in People Operations, including 5 years leadership across People Programs, People Systems, People Analytics, or a similarly complex function. Experience should include the selection and optimization of HRIS and Talent systems at small and medium- to large-sized companies. A track record of organization-wide project and program management, designing operating models, building roadmaps, and delivering cross-functional programs at scale. Implementation and development of comprehensive data analytics, reporting, and dashboarding tools for Human Resources and Talent organizations with knowledge and experience in AI-enablement for those functions. Experience managing and developing a team and building strong cross-functional partnerships. Experience designing, managing, or improving integrations across HR systems and connected People tools to support reliable data flows and scalable operations. Strong understanding of how People systems, processes, data, and employee programs fit together. Experience improving HR technology, data quality, reporting, analytics, automation, or self-service decision support. Practical experience evaluating or advancing AI use cases, with sound judgment around sensitive employee data, privacy, governance, accuracy, and human oversight. Excellent written communication, prioritization, program management, and change leadership skills. About You:  You are a strategic, systems-oriented People leader who connects technology, data, programs, and human experience. You can set organization-wide direction at the program level while engaging deeply enough to understand implementation details and remove barriers. title: Compliance Program Manager — Regulatory Compliance
description: About the team Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work. About the role As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny. Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio. You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager. In this role, you will: - Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements. - Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths. - Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments. - Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision. - Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why. - Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance. - Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners. - Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs. - Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process. - Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results. - Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes - Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed. - Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal. - Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps. - Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed. - Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership. - Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate. - Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs. - Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products.
